ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Sir John Franklin Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Pre-expedition medical for a 58-year-old naval officer chosen to command a multi-year Arctic expedition: history, examination, ECG, laboratory tests, hearing, mood, a high blood pressure reading, and a wilderness and expedition medicine consultation. Concerns: He wants to be found fit for the command, and to be fit enough to do it well; Staying well, and keeping his men well, for years beyond the reach of a doctor's office or hospital; He remembers what starvation did on an earlier journey and wants a food plan that will not fail. [S]

One tablet by mouth every morning
Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) 25 micrograms (1,000 units) oral tablet once daily, continued through the polar winters
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) 250 mg oral tablet once daily for the whole expedition, stored sealed and away from heat and light, in addition to food sources
One tablet by mouth daily from departure
Oseltamivir 75 mg oral capsule twice daily for five days
One capsule by mouth twice a day for five days

tr.td: Resting 12-lead ECG: sinus rhythm at 76, normal axis and intervals, no left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria, no Q waves
Pure tone audiometry: symmetric high-frequency sensorineural loss with a notch at 4 kHz (45 dB) on both sides; speech frequencies within 25 dB; normal tympanograms
Transthoracic echocardiogram: left ventricular ejection fraction 62%, mild concentric remodeling (septum 11 mm), normal diastolic function for age, normal valves and aortic root

Symptom-limited exercise treadmill test (Bruce protocol): 9 minutes, about 10 METs, peak heart rate 152 (94% of predicted), normal blood pressure response, no chest pain, arrhythmia or ischemic ST change
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, including his wishes for serious illness at sea or in the ice beyond the reach of evacuation
Tetanus, diphtheria and acellular pertussis (Tdap) booster
Recombinant zoster vaccine, first of two doses

list.item: Senior naval officer and Arctic explorer who has led two overland expeditions in northern Canada; lately returned from a colonial governorship that ended under public criticism; has been chosen to command a naval expedition to find the Northwest Passage, expected to last two to three years beyond any outside contact [S]
Married; one adult daughter; lives in London; widowed once, many years ago, when his first wife died of tuberculosis in the household [S]
Never smoked; a glass or two of wine with dinner on most days (AUDIT-C 3); no other substances [S]
Diet heavy in meat, bread and puddings, with few vegetables; walks most days but has done little hard exercise since his governorship; sleeps about seven hours [S]
Strengths: long experience of Arctic travel and hardship, careful scientific habits, concern for the welfare of his men, a strong religious faith, and a clear wish to be fit for the command [S]

tr.td: Pre-expedition medical for a 58-year-old naval officer chosen to command a multi-year Arctic expedition: history, examination, ECG, laboratory tests, hearing, mood, a high blood pressure reading, and a wilderness and expedition medicine consultation

Two-week review of home blood pressure readings, seen the same day by wilderness and expedition medicine: the diagnosis, treatment for years away from care, cardiac testing, nutrition, cold and evacuation
Four-week review after starting amlodipine: blood pressure, side effects, echocardiogram and urine albumin
Eight-week review: blood pressure at goal, weight, exercise treadmill test and expedition planning
Pre-departure review two weeks before sailing: blood pressure, medicines and supplies, mental health, vaccinations, the medical kit and the evacuation plan

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Pre-expedition medical: history, examination, resting ECG, kidney function and electrolytes, HbA1c, lipid panel, urine albumin, TSH, ALT, blood count, and baseline blood lead, vitamin C and vitamin D; audiogram; tuberculosis blood test because of a past household contact
Wilderness and expedition medicine consultation to advise on fitness for the command, treatment for years away from care, nutrition and food safety, cold injury, and evacuation

Blood pressure: a validated upper-arm home monitor with a large cuff, two readings morning and evening for seven days, to confirm the diagnosis; less salt, less alcohol, more vegetables and daily walking from today

Treatment: amlodipine 5 mg daily, with a goal below 130/80 mmHg at home, home readings weekly on board, and a supply for three years in blister packs; no diuretic or renin-angiotensin blocker because of dehydration, cold diuresis and no laboratory access; statin not started by his choice after a risk discussion
Heart before a strenuous remote posting: echocardiogram for stage 2 hypertension, and a symptom-limited exercise treadmill test once he has recovered from any acute illness
Weight: his own goals for walking, hill work, portions and alcohol, discussed without blame; no weight-loss medicine before departure

Nutrition and food safety for years without fresh food: vitamin C 250 mg daily in sealed, cool, dark storage, with food sources and a check of the expedition's stores; vitamin D3 daily; an energy-dense ration; canned food from suppliers without lead solder, inspected for bulging, leaking or damaged cans, which are discarded unopened; no home-canned food; a blood lead baseline

Cold: layered clothing with vapor control, dry socks and mitts, buddy checks of face, hands and feet, no tobacco or alcohol before cold exposure, rewarming of frostbite only when refreezing can be prevented, and hypothermia recognition and insulation in the field
Vaccinations, dental examination and treatment, and colorectal and other screening at the preventive visit before departure

Mind and isolation: baseline PHQ-9 and GAD-7, a routine of work, light, exercise and sleep through the polar night, a peer-support plan among the officers, and an evacuation plan with a medical kit, written instructions for the ship's surgeons, and a 12-month review of medicines
Hearing: audiogram, hearing protection around guns and engines, and seating so that his better ear faces the speaker
Confirm or exclude hypertension with a week of home readings
Home average 144/90 mmHg: stage 2 hypertension confirmed
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg at home before departure
Home average 127/79 mmHg at eight weeks on amlodipine 5 mg with lifestyle change
Lose about 5 percent of body weight before sailing by his own plan of walking, hill work and smaller portions
90.8 to 86.9 kg (4.3 percent); waist 106 to 101 cm; he counts it as met and plans to keep walking on board
Medical clearance for the command with a written expedition health plan, medical kit and evacuation plan
Cleared at the pre-departure visit with no cardiac limitation; plan, kit list and supplies in hand

list.item: Independent in all activities; walks three miles at a steady pace; climbs two flights of stairs without stopping but breathes hard; no chest pain, fainting or claudication [S]
Alert, courteous and thorough; speech normal, though he turns his better ear in a noisy room; mood good and determined; PHQ-9 3 with item 9 scored 0; GAD-7 2; no thoughts of self-harm [S]
